rows.derivation: SR4 requires, in a FUNCTION, the ANY LENGTH subject to be a BY REFERENCE formal parameter. Leg 1: the item is the function's RETURNING item (legal for a contained program by SR3 b), illegal for a function). Leg 2: the item is not in the header at all. SR1 (PIC X) and SR2 (level-1 elementary LINKAGE entry of a function) hold, so SR4 is the only violation. Rejected with COBOLNET1542 at 2002/2014/2023 (functions and ANY LENGTH are 2002+).
citations: cite.py --check 13.18.2.3 "If the source element containing the ANY LENGTH clause is a function, the subject of the entry shall be referenced in its procedure division header as a formal parameter with the BY REFERENCE phrase" -> OK §13.18.2.3 4)
rows.notes: COBOLNET1542 is shared by the SR2/SR3/SR4 placement checks in DataBinder.AnyLengthValidateUnit; the observed message is the SR4 text. A third leg (BY VALUE formal) was dropped: it also violates §14.2.2 SR2 (COBOLNET1553, BY VALUE needs a numeric/pointer class), so it would not be a single-rule negative. The positive (BY REFERENCE formal) leg is already conformance:2002/any_length_function.

rows.derivation: Positive: one outer program with `ARITHMETIC NATIVE` (IS omitted) and three contained programs with `ARITHMETIC STANDARD-DECIMAL` (IS omitted), `ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-DECIMAL`, `ARITHMETIC IS NATIVE`. Each computes SQRT(2) into 9V9(30). SD: sqrt(2) to 34 digits = 1.414213562373095048801688724209698 (next digit 0, so every rounding mode agrees) -> truncated 1414213562373095048801688724209. A binary64 (native) result differs from the 17th digit, so a clause ignored or misparsed changes the line. Native is implementor-defined, so only a 1E-6 window is pinned. Negatives: two alternatives (plain braces = exactly one) -> COBOL0307 at 2014/2023; no alternative -> COBOL0001 at 2002/2014/2023.

rows.derivation: `IF A = B AND NOT NOT C`: by §8.8.4.12.4 GR1 the subject and operator are inserted, giving (A = B) AND NOT NOT (A = C). Table 5 lets NOT be followed only by a simple-condition or '(' (its NOTE: 'the pair NOT NOT is not permissible'), so the insertion result breaks Table 5. Everything else is valid (the control `A = B AND NOT C` compiles and runs), so rejection is owed at 85/2002/2014/2023; observed COBOL0001 at all four.
citations: cite.py --check 8.8.4.12.3 "The result of implied insertion shall comply with the rules of Table 5" -> OK §8.8.4.12.3 2)
cite.py --check 8.8.4.12.4 "The effect of using abbreviations is as if the last preceding stated subject were inserted in place of the omitted subject" -> OK §8.8.4.12.4 1)
cite.py --check 8.8.4.11.3 "the pair 'NOT (' is permissible while the pair 'NOT NOT' is not permissible" -> OK §8.8.4.11.3
rows.notes: The adjudicator's second probe `A = B AND NOT NOT < C` was NOT used. It can be read as NOT followed by the extended operator 'NOT <', which expands to (A = B) AND NOT (A NOT < C), and that complies with Table 5. It is rejected by the general format (and by the §8.8.4.12.4 NOTE), not by SR2, so it would not be a single-rule witness.

rows.derivation: Receivers with no V, '.' or P have their point after the rightmost digit (r3), and r4 aligns on it. 123.456 -> 9(5) = 00123; 9(3)V9(3) 987.654 -> 9(5) = 00987; 0.5 -> 99 = 00; 12345.9 -> 999 = 345 (high-order cut); 7.9 -> ZZ9 (edited, no point) = '  7'; 123.99 -> 9B99 = '1 23'. A point anywhere else would move the digits.

rows.derivation: Pins the documented choice (CONFORMANCE.md DOC-A.1-6: always coincident, no slack). 85: G = (9(4) COMP, X): LENGTH 3. Through a REDEFINES, G1 := 0 appears as LOW-VALUES in bytes 1-2 (true in either byte order) and G2 := 'Z' is byte 3. D = (X(2), 9(3)) <- 'XY123' gives D1=XY, D2=123, LENGTH 5. 2002: BYTE-LENGTH of strongly-typed (N, X) = 3, alphanumeric (N, X) = 3 (national = 2 bytes, item 33), (1(3) BIT, X) = 2 (the display item is on the next byte boundary, §8.5.1.6.1), strongly-typed (X(2), X(3)) = 5.
citations: cite.py --check 8.5.1.6.1 "The alignment of the start of an alphanumeric group item relative to the first item within that group is defined by the implementor" -> OK §8.5.1.6.1
